name: open-babel
why: Chemical file format converter and toolbox; a real door into molecular structure formats you can run at home.

brief.what_it_is: Open Babel is a chemical toolbox for reading, writing, converting, searching and analyzing molecular data. It ships ready-to-use command-line programs plus a programmer's toolkit. The README says it reads, writes and converts over 90 chemical file formats, while the project website says over 110. It can filter and search molecular files with SMARTS and other methods, and generate 2D and 3D coordinates for inputs such as SMILES and InChI. The brew executable list (obabel, obgen, obminimize and others) comes from the package metadata; I did not see those program names in the README or website.
brief.why_it_exists: The project describes itself as designed to speak the many languages of chemical data, and as an open, collaborative effort that lets anyone search, convert, analyze or store data from molecular modeling, chemistry, solid-state materials, biochemistry and related fields.
brief.standout: One toolbox covers a very wide span of chemical file formats and fields, from molecular modeling to solid-state and nuclear chemistry, and it comes both as command-line programs and as a library for programmers. The website says it has been downloaded over 700,000 times and is used by over 40 related projects.
brief.status: Active on the evidence available. The website's documentation is labelled openbabel-3-2-0, and the README has release and download badges. I did not see a last-release or last-commit date in either page, so the exact recency is unknown.
brief.caveats: Licensed under the GNU GPL version 2, so anything you build on it inherits those terms. The README and website disagree on the format count (over 90 versus over 110). The README names no command lines, so the program list above is unverified from the pages I read. I did not check install or build requirements beyond brew, and the brew caveats field is empty.
